original_question: Let nu_w = S_w(1, ..., 1) be the principal evaluation of the Schubert polynomial of w, and let u(n) be the maximum of nu_w over w in S_n. Determine sharper asymptotic bounds for u(n), in particular whether there is a constant alpha with 1/4 <= alpha <= 1/2 such that u(n) is asymptotic to 2^(alpha n^2).
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 11 (page 2): the open problem on the maximal principal evaluation of Schubert polynomials, defining nu_w = S_w(1, ..., 1), u(n) = max_{w in S_n} nu_w, and asking for better asymptotic bounds on u(n). This is the exact target of the draft. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))
correct_elements: The draft already captures the core content of Problem 11 almost verbatim: nu_w as the principal evaluation of the Schubert polynomial S_w, u(n) as the maximum over w in S_n, and the asymptotic question of whether u(n) behaves like 2^(alpha n^2) for some alpha in [1/4, 1/2]. It also correctly stays with Problem 11 rather than drifting to the separate nearby questions about which permutations maximize nu_w or what their limiting shape might be. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))
missing_details: The paper explicitly says that nu_w = S_w(1, ..., 1) is the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial S_w of the permutation w; adding this removes ambiguity about how many variables are being specialized to 1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))

To make the question fully stand-alone, the quantifiers should be explicit: for each integer n >= 1, with S_n the symmetric group on n letters, define u(n) = max_{w in S_n} nu_w. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))

The paper frames the problem against the asymptotic inequalities 1/4 <= liminf_{n->infty} log_2 u(n)/n^2 <= limsup_{n->infty} log_2 u(n)/n^2 <= 1/2, and then records sharper cited bounds 0.2932362762... below and 0.37 above; including this context makes the question more faithful to the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))

If the phrase 'u(n) is asymptotic to 2^(alpha n^2)' is retained, it is best to spell out that this means u(n)/2^(alpha n^2) -> 1 as n -> infty. The paper states the asymptotic form but leaves that meaning implicit. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency hypothesis belongs here; Problem 11 is purely a combinatorial asymptotic question, so adding such data would distort the paper's scope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1, let S_n be the symmetric group on n letters. For each permutation w in S_n, let S_w denote the Schubert polynomial of w, and define nu_w := S_w(1, ..., 1), equivalently the sum of the coefficients of S_w. Let u(n) := max_{w in S_n} nu_w. Determine sharper asymptotic bounds for u(n): in particular, determine the exponential growth rate of u(n) on the scale 2^(c n^2), and decide whether there exists a constant alpha with 1/4 <= alpha <= 1/2 such that u(n) ~ 2^(alpha n^2) as n -> infty. The paper records the baseline bounds 1/4 <= liminf_{n->infty} log_2 u(n)/n^2 <= limsup_{n->infty} log_2 u(n)/n^2 <= 1/2, together with cited improvements of the lower bound to about 0.2932362762 and the upper bound to 0.37. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.25446))
